subject: Computer Science and Engineering
topic: Computer Organization and Architecture - Unit IV (Memory/Paging)

questions.stem: Which of the following correctly describes the role of main memory in program execution?
options: Main memory stores program instructions so the CPU can fetch and execute them.
Main memory retains data permanently even when the computer is powered off.
Main memory only holds temporary data, not program code, during execution.
Secondary memory holds the instructions that the CPU executes directly.
questions.correctAnswer: Main memory stores program instructions so the CPU can fetch and execute them.

stemAnswerAlignment.responsivenessAnalysis: Option A directly states that main memory stores program instructions so the CPU can fetch and execute them, which precisely answers the question asking for the correct description of main memory's role.

questions.stem: When the CPU stores a value to address 0xFF00 that is mapped to a UART, how does the operation differ between memory‑mapped I/O and isolated I/O?
options: Only the memory write line activates, leaving the I/O device unchanged
The CPU must issue a special I/O instruction to affect the device
A dedicated I/O write line activates, but the memory location is untouched
The same write line drives both memory and I/O, performing the device write
questions.correctAnswer: The same write line drives both memory and I/O, performing the device write

stemAnswerAlignment.responsivenessAnalysis: The keyed option D explains that the same write line is used for both memory and the UART, directly addressing how the operation differs from isolated I/O which would require a separate mechanism.
